money.note: Individuals gave $2,316,580; PAC money $427,341; candidate's own money $25. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Lawyer and former teacher and deputy attorney general. California Assembly member for District 6 from 2016 to 2022. Ran in the 2021 governor recall. U.S. House member since 2023, first as a Republican, then an independent from March 2026. Ran in District 6 as No Party Preference.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include former U.S. Sen. Joe Manchin III (Independent), the Forward Party, Alliance for American Leadership and Reform California.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Kiley was born or when he moved to California; sources only say he grew up in the Sacramento area. We found no documented stances on data centers, development or growth limits, and no documented actions or statements on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, gun laws, or abortion. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties in the pages we could read. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys, so we have no questionnaire answers from him. The Ballotpedia page we received was cut off partway through the state scorecards list.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.bio: Pediatrician and UC Davis professor who also owns a small business. Served in the California State Assembly (2010–2014) and State Senate (2014–2022), where he chaired the Senate Health Committee. Ran for Sacramento mayor in 2024. Won the U.S. House seat for California's 6th District in 2026.

endorsements.text: Endorsed in the 2026 race by U.S. Rep. Ro Khanna, the California Federation of Labor Unions, the California Teachers Association, the National Union of Healthcare Workers, Equality California, and The Sacramento Bee.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions from Pan on data centers or on new development, and nothing on homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, school choice or voucher programs, or support for police pay and pensions. We found no record of when he moved to California. His campaign site gives general statements on guns, abortion and immigration, but we found no specific bills or actions in the sources we had. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties.

qual.background: Pediatrician and UC Davis associate professor who led its pediatric residency program. He served in the California State Assembly (2010–2014) and State Senate (2014–2022), and he authored SB 277, the 2015 school vaccination law. He also co-owns a small business.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says that in Congress he will work for universal background checks and an assault weapons ban, and that he will support secure firearm storage.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he will work to codify Roe v. Wade and that Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California rated him 100%.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site says he supports a path to citizenship and wants ICE overhauled and replaced with a different agency. It says immigrants are vital to the economy and to innovation.
